KMSpico is one of the most widely recognized unofficial software activation tools. It is commonly associated with activating Microsoft Windows and Microsoft Office products without purchasing a valid license for free.
Because of its ability to bypass the normal activation process, KMSpico has attracted considerable attention over the years. Its popularity online gives people trust that it is a safe solution, while others warn that it can contain viruses, steal personal information from your compter, or even damage an operating system to became unusable...
Windows Defender and other antivirus applications may also detect KMSpico and it's related files as threats, which raises an important question:
Is KMSpico actually a virus, or are antivirus warnings simply caused by the way it works?
In this article, we will talk about what is KMSpico and how it works, why system securities software detects it as a threat, what are the risks of downloading unofficial activation tools, and what you should do if you have already installed one or still using.
What Is KMSpico? KMSpico is an unofficial and 3rd party implemented app that bypasses Microsoft's standart activation process.
It is associated with Microsoft's Key Management Service (KMS), which takes it's name from... A legitimate activation technology developed for organizations that manage large numbers of Windows and Office installations.
In a typical KMS setup, a company runs its own activation server, and computers connected to its network regularly communicate with that server to keep their Windows or Office licenses activated and their activations are up to date or expired...
Unofficial KMS activation tools attempt to imitate parts of this process. KMSpico is commonly described as using a local KMS emulator to make Windows or Office behave as though it has been activated through a volume licensing environment.
However, this does not mean that the user has obtained a genuine license. An activation status displayed by Windows is not proof that the underlying license is legitimate.
Why Does Windows Defender Detect KMSpico? One of the most common reasons people search for KMSpico is that Windows Defender or another antivirus application identifies it as malware.
There are several reasons for this behavior.
1. It Bypasses the Normal Activation Process KMSpico is designed to interfere with Microsoft's normal activation mechanisms. Tools that modify activation related settings, services, or system behavior can trigger security software.
Antivirus products use different detection methods, including:
Signature-based detection
Heuristic analysis
Behavioral monitoring
Reputation and cloud-based protection
Potentially unwanted application (PUA) detection
Consequently, an unofficial activation tool may be detected even when a particular detection does not establish that the file is actively stealing data or destroying files.
2. It May Require Elevated System Permissions Activation utilities may request administrator privileges because they attempt to modify system-level settings or interact with Windows services.
This is particularly important from a security perspective.
A program running with administrator privileges can potentially make significant changes to a computer. If a malicious version is executed with these permissions, the consequences can be much more serious than those of an ordinary application.
3. Its Distribution Is Difficult to Verify KMSpico has been distributed through many unofficial websites, download portals, archives, and file-sharing platforms.
There is no reliable way to make sure a version/release downloaded from a source is original or not, so it makes the KMSpico untrusted. 
A download may have been modified, repackaged, or bundled with additional programs without both the user's and developer's knowledge.
This is one of the most important security concerns associated with unofficial activation tools.
Can KMSpico Contain a Virus or Malware? Yes. Files distributed under the KMSpico name can contain malware.
Unofficial software downloads are a common way for malicious actors to distribute unwanted programs. A user may believe they are downloading an activation utility while actually receiving an executable that contains additional malicious functionality.
Depending on the particular file, potential threats may include:
Information stealers: Malware designed to collect information from your Browser and other storage of your Computer. Like browser cache... Passwords, your Credit Card info... 
Trojans: Malicious programs that get in your system as a safe, authentic program.
RATs (Remote Access Trojans): Virus/Malware that can let your Pc to be controlled from unwanted people (developer of the virus)
Cryptocurrency miners: Programs that will use your system resources and use them for mining cryptocurrency, will cause your system became unstable and overheat. 
Downloaders: Malware that makes your pc to download and auto install malwares like ad viruses or self promoting apps (Unwanted apps that people distrubute their apps using viruses). 
These are examples of threats that can accompany unofficial downloads. They should not be interpreted as proof that every KMSpico copy contains all, or any, of these threats.
The important distinction is that you cannot assume a KMSpico download is safe simply because it carries a familiar name or looks like a previously used version.
Is KMSpico a False Positive? Not necessarily.
A false positive occurs when antivirus software incorrectly identifies a legitimate or harmless file as malicious.
However, an antivirus detection should not automatically be dismissed as a false positive just because the program is an activation tool.
Some detections may be related to suspicious activation behavior or potentially unwanted software. Others may indicate genuinely malicious code.
The exact detection name and the file being scanned matter.
For example, a security product may classify a file as:
A potentially unwanted application
A hacktool or unauthorized activation utility
A suspicious or potentially malicious executable
A Trojan or another specific malware family
These classifications do not all mean the same thing.
It is also important to understand that antivirus products use different detection engines. One scanner detecting a file does not automatically establish that it is dangerous, but multiple consistent malware detections should be taken seriously.
My recommendation is not to disable Windows Defender or ignore its warnings just to run an unofficial activation utility. 
How to Check Whether a KMSpico File Is Malicious If you have already downloaded a suspicious executable, you can use reputable security services to obtain additional information about it.
One commonly used service is VirusTotal.
VirusTotal allows users to submit files or search for file hashes and see results from multiple antivirus engines.
However, there are some important limitations:
A clean antivirus scan result does not guarantee that a file is safe. It can still contain some implementation parts that can be unsafe..
Antivirus programs can differ in performance of a file is malicious or not
Detection names may differ between different security vendors.
A file may be modified after a previous scan, making you need to re-scan again.
Uploading a file to a public analysis service may expose that file to security researchers and participating partners.
For these reasons, VirusTotal should be treated as an additional analysis resource, not as a guarantee of safety.
You should never execute a suspicious file simply because it receives a low detection score.
What Should You Do If You Have Already Installed KMSpico? If you have installed KMSpico and are now concerned about your computer's security, there are several sensible steps you can take.
1. Run a Microsoft Defender Scan Open Windows Security and navigate to:
Virus & threat protection → Scan options
Start with a full scan.
If you suspect that malware that you think that it gained administrator privileges or is difficult to remove, consider running Microsoft Defender Offline. This performs a scan outside the normal Windows environment.
2. Remove Suspicious Software Uninstall KMSpico and any other suspicious unfamiliar applications that appeared around the same time.
Do not assume that uninstalling the activation utility automatically removes every additional program that may have been installed alongside it.
3. Review Startup Applications Check Task Manager's Startup apps section and look for unfamiliar applications including background processes. 
You can also take a look at installed programs and scheduled tasks if you notice any suspicious activity.
Do not delete/stop any Windows Service since they work for security of your Computer and personal data...
4. Change Important Passwords if Necessary If you executed an untrusted file and suspect an information stealer or other credential-stealing malware, change important passwords from a separate, known-clean device.
Prioritize your email, Microsoft account, banking services, and other accounts containing sensitive information.
Enable multifactor authentication wherever possible.
5. Consider a Clean Windows Installation If you still think that your computer is still virussed, urgently backup your important data, photos, documents etc... And directly consider a clean Windows Installation. Make sure to use an USB which not inserted to your old Infected Operating System. Theese viruses can spread to USB too, in order to spread it to other computers...
Legal Alternatives to KMSpico If you want to activate Windows or Microsoft Office without exposing your computer to unofficial activation tools, there are legitimate alternatives.
Windows Licenses Microsoft offers different Windows licensing options depending on the edition and intended use.
You can check your activation status under:
Settings → System → Activation
For purchasing or resolving licensing issues, use Microsoft's official website or an authorized retailer.
Microsoft Office and Microsoft 365 For Office applications, Microsoft offers Microsoft 365 subscriptions and other licensing options depending on the product and region.
You can also check and downlad free alternatives such as:
LibreOffice
Microsoft 365 for the web
Google Docs
These options may be sufficient if you mainly need word processing, spreadsheets, or presentations.
Be careful with unusually cheap product keys sold by unknown online marketplaces. A low price alone does not establish that a license is genuine, transferable, or supported by Microsoft.
What About Simply Removing the Activate Windows Watermark? Some users are not particularly concerned about activation itself. They just want to get rid of the watermark we see at right down "Activate Windows". It is done from registry or powershell without any 3rd party software...
However, hiding an activation message does not activate Windows or create a valid license.
The underlying activation status remains unchanged, and certain modifications may stop working after Windows updates.
If Windows is not activated, the appropriate solution is to resolve the activation issue through Microsoft's official activation settings and licensing support.
Final Thoughts: Is KMSpico Safe? KMSpico is an unofficial activation utility associated with bypassing Microsoft's normal Windows and Office activation process.
Although antivirus detections do not always prove that a particular file contains active malware, it would be equally misleading to claim that KMSpico is completely harmless.
There are several reasons to be cautious:
Its unofficial distribution makes file authenticity difficult to establish.
Some downloads may be modified or bundled with malware.
Activation-related modifications can trigger security software.
Running unknown programs with administrator privileges creates additional security risks.
Using unofficial activation tools does not provide a legitimate Microsoft license.
In my opinion, the potential security and licensing risks are not worth taking just to avoid purchasing a legitimate license. You can check online for one time use cheap keys from trusted sellers... 
If you already have KMSpico installed, do not panic. A detection does not automatically mean that your computer is infected. However, you should take security warnings seriously, scan your system, and avoid running untrusted activation software.
Frequently Asked Questions Is KMSpico a virus? KMSpico is an unofficial activation utility, not a conventional computer virus by definition. However, files distributed under its name can be modified or bundled with malware. Its safety cannot be guaranteed.
Can KMSpico steal passwords? A malicious executable distributed as KMSpico could contain an information stealer capable of collecting passwords, browser cookies, and other sensitive information. This does not establish that every copy has this functionality.
Why does Windows Defender delete KMSpico? Windows Defender may detect activation tools because of their suspicious behavior, system modifications, or association with potentially unwanted software. Some files may also contain genuine malware.
Can KMSpico damage Windows? A malicious or incorrectly functioning version could modify system components, install unwanted services, or interfere with normal system operation. However, it is not accurate to claim that every KMSpico installation will damage Windows.
Is KMSpico safe if VirusTotal shows zero detections? No. Zero detections do not guarantee that a file is safe. New, modified, or previously unseen malware may not yet be recognized by antivirus engines.
Does KMSpico provide a genuine Windows license? No. An unofficial activation utility does not provide a legitimate Microsoft product license, even if Windows displays an activated status.

Why You Should NOT Buy Fake AirPods in 2026: The Truth About Replica Earbuds Fake AirPods have become increasingly sophisticated over the last few years. What once looked like an obvious cheap imitation has evolved into something much more convincing. Some replicas now feature surprisingly good sound quality, AirPods-style pairing animations, battery indicators, and even compatibility with certain Apple device features.
At first glance, buying a pair of replica AirPods for a fraction of the original price might seem like a great deal. After all, why spend a significant amount of money on genuine Apple AirPods when a much cheaper alternative appears to offer a similar experience?
I used to think about this differently as well.
I have personally owned replica AirPods, a pair of Airpods 3 with charging case, branded as “Fubar Airpods 3” bought from Turkey. Surprisingly, the experience was not entirely bad. The sound quality was quite good, and the earbuds were recognized by Apple devices almost like genuine AirPods. Also find my Apple was working when you connected the Fake Airpods 3 to an Apple Device…
However, after looking beyond the initial experience, I believe there are several important reasons why buying counterfeit AirPods is not a good decision.
This article is not about promoting replica products or recommending specific counterfeit models. Instead, I want to explain how these products work, why some of them are surprisingly convincing, what their technical limitations are, and why I would recommend choosing legitimate budget TWS earbuds instead.
1. What Are These Fake AirPods and Why They Became So Popular? Fake AirPods are wireless earbuds designed to imitate Apple’s original AirPods. They may copy the appearance of the earbuds, charging case, packaging, product names, and even some of the software features.
You may see descriptions at online shopping stores like:
1:1 AirPods replica
OEM AirPods
High-copy AirPods
Clone AirPods
Replica AirPods Pro
AirPods 3 replicas
These terms are often used loosely by sellers and do not necessarily describe a specific hardware platform or quality level.
It is also important to distinguish between generic TWS earbuds and counterfeit AirPods.
TWS stands for True Wireless Stereo. It simply describes wireless earbuds that operate without a cable connecting the left and right sides. TWS doesnt have any implementation made or mimic Apple Airpods Products. Just think like a classic cheap bluetooth wirelles in ear twin headphones. There are many legitimate manufacturers producing affordable TWS earbuds. These products may have a similar general design to AirPods without pretending to be genuine Apple products.
Counterfeit AirPods are different. They attempt to imitate Apple’s branding and product identity, potentially misleading buyers into believing that they are purchasing something manufactured or authorized by Apple.
Their popularity is understandable. Genuine AirPods can be expensive, while replicas are marketed at considerably lower prices.
But the low price does not necessarily mean good value.
2. Not All Fake AirPods Use the Same Hardware One common misconception is that every replica AirPods model uses the same cheap Bluetooth chip and offers equally poor performance.
Inside of an Original Apple Airpods
That is not necessarily true.
The replica market has evolved, and different products can use different Bluetooth audio platforms. Some inexpensive models use basic solutions, while more sophisticated versions have been associated with chipset families such as Airoha, Huilian, and BES.
These platforms help explain why certain replicas can offer surprisingly convincing connectivity and audio features.
However, identifying and knowing the chipset alone is not enough to determine the quality and performance of an entire product itself.
Airoha Bluetooth Chipsets Airoha is one of the manufacturers frequently mentioned in discussions about more advanced AirPods replicas.
Chipset names and variants reported in different replica generations include:
Airoha 1562M
Airoha 1562E
Airoha 1563E
Airoha 1571AM
Some community documentation associates these chipsets with different AirPods-style replica versions.
Airoha 1562A equipped replica Airpods Pro from Aliexpress
Depending on the implementation, Airoha-based platforms can offer relatively advanced Bluetooth connectivity, audio processing, power management, and support for additional features.
This is one reason why some replicas perform considerably better than basic generic Bluetooth earbuds.
However, a product using an Airoha chipset is not automatically high quality. The speaker drivers, microphones, firmware, battery cells, antenna design, and overall manufacturing process are equally important.
It is also worth noting that chipset names used in replica communities do not always correspond directly to official manufacturer product names. Exact hardware identification can vary between models and production batches.
Huilian Chipsets and Apple-Like Integration Huilian is another chipset family that appears in discussions about more sophisticated AirPods replicas.
Names such as Huilian A10 and Huilian 247 have been associated with products offering advanced iOS-style integration.
Huilian 247 equipped Airpods Pro 3 from a Russian seller…
Some implementations reportedly support AirPods-like pairing experiences and features resembling Apple’s multi-device functionality.
This can make certain replicas surprisingly convincing when used with an iPhone.
However, similar-looking software behavior does not mean that a product has genuine Apple hardware or access to every proprietary Apple service.
BES (Bestechnic) Chipsets BES is another manufacturer associated with Bluetooth audio platforms used in different wireless earbuds.
Examples reported in replica discussions include:
BES 2300ZP
BES 2500YP
BES 2600 series
Some implementations are associated with more advanced audio processing and noise-cancellation capabilities.
Nevertheless, chipset specifications alone cannot guarantee effective ANC, good microphone quality, or long-term reliability.
A poorly designed product can still perform badly even if it uses a relatively advanced Bluetooth chipset.
Jieli and Bluetrum: Other Bluetooth Solutions Not every replica uses a relatively advanced platform.
Jieli (JL) and Bluetrum are also associated with affordable Bluetooth audio products and entry-level wireless earbuds.
These platforms can provide basic wireless audio functionality, although the actual performance depends on the complete hardware and firmware implementation.
It is important not to judge a product’s quality, performance etc… directly by its chipset. The quality matters by the whole implemention of product including chipset, speakers, microphone and the battery case. A cheaper Bluetooth platform does not automatically mean terrible sound quality, just as a more expensive platform does not guarantee a good listening experience.
The biggest issue is the lack of reliable information and quality control surrounding many counterfeit products.
3. How Can Fake AirPods Device Can Appear as Genuine AirPods on an iPhone? This is probably one of the most interesting aspects of modern AirPods replicas.
If not equipped as a TWS device or any other trash quality chipsetted Airpods Replica, when you open the case of your replica Airpods, it interacts with Iphone and shows Airpods opening animation, device model (like original), device name and battery percentage…
For an inexperienced user or 3rd party inspectors, this can create the impression that the earbuds contain Apple’s original hardware.
But there is an important distinction.
An iPhone device displaying an AirPods-style openning and pairing window does not prove that the earbuds contain an Apple H1 or H2 chip. Shortly doesnt mean that Airpods device is original. A seller showing Replica Airpods Pro connected to An Iphone device with Airpods Pairing Animation…
Certain Bluetooth/Wifi implementations and mimiced design of hardware/firmware configurations can imitate parts of an Original Apple Airpods and device-identification…
This is why some replicas can appear surprisingly authentic during initial setup.
However, genuine AirPods offer much deeper integration with Apple’s ecosystem.
For example, seeing an AirPods-style pairing animation does not establish that a replica has:
Genuine Apple H1 or H2 hardware
Full Apple Find My network integration
Genuine iCloud device association
All original AirPods software features
The same security and authentication mechanisms
A familiar interface is not proof of authenticity.
Also dont forget that some non cheap priced AirPods Replicas come with Magsafe support but still this doesnt mean that Replica Airpods do include Original Apple Hardware. Dont forget that these specifications can be replicated with low prices today…
This is also why I would never recommend buying a product simply because an online seller demonstrates an iPhone pairing animation in a promotional video.
4. My Personal Experience With Replica Fubar AirPods 3 I want to mention my own experience because not every replica experience is necessarily terrible.
I previously owned a pair of Fubar AirPods 3, and honestly, I was surprised by their performance.
The sound quality was quite good, especially considering that they were not genuine Apple products. Sadly microphone quality was trash, but I do use phone’s own microphone during daily talks and other jobs… Another interesting aspect was their compatibility with Apple devices. During pairing, they were recognized almost like original AirPods, providing a familiar experience that was considerably more convincing than what I expected from a cheap imitation.
This is an important distinction.
I am not claiming that every fake AirPods product has terrible sound quality or that every replica is unusable.
Some versions can offer a surprisingly decent experience, particularly when they use more advanced Bluetooth audio platforms.
This is my Fubar AirPods 3. Bought from Turkey online. The box doesnt have Apple logo only writes Airpods 3 with MagSafe support. Replicated Apple marks but doesnt have any Apple logo on box and charging case…
Since I use Samsung Galaxy S23 FE, I directly opened case of my Fubar Airpods 3, pressed the button and Android Bluetooth directly recognised my Rep Airpods with name "AirPods" comes as default. Pressed on connect and it directly paired without any problem. Iphone Devices did recognised the Fubar Airpods 3 directly when I opened case and connected with animation of Original Airpods 3. This is PodsBattery app which recognised battery level of my Fubar Airpods 3. However, I cannot confirm the exact chipset installed in my particular Fubar AirPods 3. It had no any chip information from seller. Without dismantling and inspecting the internal circuit board or obtaining reliable manufacturer documentation, identifying it as an Airoha, Huilian, or BES model would be speculation.
Since I used Android Device (S23 FE) I monitored battery using 3rd party Original/Rep Airpods and TWS control program installed using APK file Online or Directly from Google Play. But phone itself did warned when battery get too low (<%10)...
Even if a replica works well initially, that does not remove the other problems associated with counterfeit products.
In my opinion, a product should be judged not only by its first impression but also by its reliability, durability, safety, and the support available after purchase.
And this is where many replicas become difficult to recommend.
As an update, 2 to 3 months later, the left airpods did started to lose sound. And about 5 months later total, the left airpods did lose connection completely and the product became trash. 
5. Sound Quality: Some Replicas Are Surprisingly Good, But Consistency Matters Sound quality is one of the most important factors when purchasing wireless earbuds.
As my Fubar AirPods 3 experience demonstrates, some replicas can sound surprisingly good.
However, this does not mean that the entire replica market offers consistent audio performance.
Depending on the product, you may encounter:
Weak or uncontrolled bass
Muddy midrange frequencies
Harsh or overly sharp treble
Distortion at higher volumes
Poor or zero stereo separation that gives mono sound on both pair
Different sound levels between earbuds which give trash experience
The biggest problem is inconsistency.
Two products advertised with similar descriptions may use completely different drivers, chipsets, and firmware according to the production batch difference.
You also cannot reliably determine sound quality from the seller's product photographs or specifications. Maybe from the comments from previous buyers, review star average...
Legitimate budget TWS manufacturers generally provide more identifiable product information and offer a better opportunity to find independent reviews.
You do not need to spend a fortune to get decent sound quality. 
You simply need a product from a manufacturer that stands behind what it sells.
6. Battery Life and Charging Reliability Battery performance is another area where inexpensive counterfeit earbuds can become problematic.
Wireless earbuds contain small rechargeable batteries, and the charging case contains an additional battery.
Their performance depends on several factors:
Battery cell quality
Charging circuit design
Power management
Firmware optimization
Manufacturing consistency
Some replicas may initially offer acceptable battery life but become less reliable after repeated charging cycles.
Potential problems include:
One earbud draining faster than the other
Inaccurate battery percentage readings
Charging cases losing capacity quickly
Earbuds failing to charge consistently
Unexpected shutdowns
There is also a safety consideration.
Lithium-ion batteries require trusted charging protection and thermal control. Poorly manufactured or inadequately protected battery systems can overheating, swelling and create fire hazard.
This does not mean that every inexpensive wireless earbud is dangerous.
However, when buying a Replica product you need to know that it doesnt have certificates for safety. 
Saving money is not particularly useful if the product becomes unreliable or potentially unsafe.
7. Fake ANC and Misleading Product Features Active Noise Cancellation (ANC) is one of the most attractive features of modern wireless earbuds.
It uses microphones and electronic processing to reduce certain types of environmental noise.
Unfortunately, some replica products advertise features such as:
Active Noise Cancellation
Transparency Mode
Spatial Audio
Adaptive Audio
Environmental Noise Cancellation
But a feature name (like %100 ANC/ENC) printed on a product listing does not guarantee that the function works as expected. Also they are probably not printed, just extrally sticked to the box/gelatin of product to show customers it has equipped with ANC. Also they do this to show the product has fake warranty too... In Turkey (as my experience) these replica Airpods 4 ANC's are sold for 8 USD, logically can you think that you can get a working ANC feature for 8 Bucks? 
Cheap Replica Airpods 4 with probably fake ANC Sticker on box...
It is also important to distinguish between active noise cancellation and passive noise isolation.
Passive isolation comes from the physical fit of the earbuds and their ear tips.
ANC uses microphones and signal processing to reduce external sounds. ANC is a specification which requires professional and reliable implementation. 
Some inexpensive earbuds may offer basic passive isolation but very limited active noise cancellation.
Without credible specifications and independent measurements, it is difficult to know what you are actually getting.
A convincing feature list is not the same as a properly implemented feature.
8. Microphone Quality and Everyday Usability Wireless earbuds are not only used for listening to music.
Since these earbuds are practical for daily and job use, many people rely on them for phone calls, Discord, online meetings, and video calls.
Microphone quality can be a weak point in some replica products.
Potential problems include:
Muffled voice recordings
Excessive background noise
Poor outdoor call quality
Inconsistent microphone volume
Unnatural voice processing
A pair of earbuds may sound acceptable when playing music but perform poorly when you use the microphone.
This is particularly frustrating because microphone quality is difficult to judge from promotional photographs and short product videos.
If you regularly make calls or attend online meetings, a legitimate budget product with independent microphone tests is a much safer choice.
9. Bluetooth Connectivity and Software Reliability Bluetooth connectivity is another important part of the wireless earbud experience.
Some advanced replicas offer surprisingly good pairing and connection stability. Others can become frustrating after regular use.
Potential problems include:
Random Bluetooth disconnections
One earbud failing to connect
Audio synchronization problems
Unreliable automatic pairing
Inaccurate battery indicators
Compatibility problems after smartphone updates
Some products also imitate Apple's pairing interface and battery pop-ups.
However, these features do not guarantee that the internal software is maintained or that future smartphone updates will not introduce compatibility issues.
TWS equipped rep airpods never have Airpods Pairing animation at iphones, only generic Bluetooth connection both on Apple and other devices... 
Generic Bluetooth connection of TWS earbuds on iphone bluetooth settings...
There is a major difference between successfully imitating a feature today and providing reliable software support over several years.
10. Build Quality, Durability and Warranty Support The initial appearance of a replica can be surprisingly convincing.
The charging case may look similar to the original, the earbuds may feel reasonably solid, and the packaging may imitate Apple's design.
But appearance is not a reliable indicator of long-term durability.
Potential problems include:
Loose charging contacts
Weak case hinges
Damaged charging ports
Earbuds that stop charging
Worn-out batteries
Unreliable touch controls
Another important issue is after-sales support.
With a genuine product or a legitimate budget earbud from an established manufacturer, you generally have a clearer route to warranty service, replacement, and technical support.
With an unknown counterfeit product, support may be limited or completely unavailable.
If something breaks after a few months, you may have no practical way to repair or replace it.
This is one of the biggest reasons I would avoid counterfeit electronics, even when their initial performance seems acceptable.
11. Not All Fake AirPods Are Sold as Apple Products Another category worth discussing is branded AirPods replicas.
Unlike products that directly use Apple's logo and packaging, these earbuds are sometimes sold under their own brand names or alternative product names. They may use almost identical designs, similar charging cases, and marketing language that deliberately reminds customers of Apple's AirPods.
Subzero Air 3 Wirelles Airpoids. Replica airpods selling as branded by "Subzero". Warranty may apply...
Some of these products have appeared in international markets under names such as WhitePods, ColorPods, and other AirPods-inspired branding.
Their packaging may look different from Apple's, but the product itself can still be designed to imitate the appearance and perceived experience of genuine AirPods.
This distinction is important: a product carrying another company's brand is not automatically a counterfeit Apple product.
There are legitimate wireless earbuds from established manufacturers that offer similar designs and features. However, some lesser-known brands use this approach to make generic or replica hardware appear more established and trustworthy than it really is.
The main concern is transparency.
Who actually manufactures the earbuds? Which chipset and Bluetooth platform do they use? Are the advertised battery capacity, noise cancellation, microphone quality, and water-resistance claims independently verified? Does the company provide firmware updates, replacement parts, customer support, and a meaningful warranty?
A brand name printed on a charging case does not automatically answer these questions.
Even if a particular pair sounds surprisingly good or connects to an iPhone with an AirPods-like pop-up, that does not establish that it offers the same hardware, software support, or long-term reliability as a genuine product.
For this reason, consumers should look beyond the branding and promotional claims.
A clearly identified, independently reviewed budget earbud from a reputable manufacturer is generally a more transparent choice than an imitation product whose actual manufacturer and specifications are difficult to verify.
It is also important not to confuse these products with legitimate alternatives from companies such as JBL, Sony, Samsung, or OnePlus. Similar design language does not automatically make a product counterfeit.
12. Screen-Equipped Fake AirPods: When the Charging Case Has a Display One of the more unusual developments in the replica earbud market is the introduction of charging cases with built-in displays.
Some modified AirPods-style replicas feature a small touchscreen integrated into the charging case. Instead of using only a smartphone, users can interact directly with the case to access different settings and information.
Replica Modified Airpods Pro 2 with ANC, Sound, Battery Monitor etc...
Depending on the model, the display may show:
Left and right earbud battery levels
Charging case battery percentage
Bluetooth connection status
Noise cancellation and transparency options
Equalizer presets
Device information and additional shortcuts
Custom wallpapers and visual themes
Some versions even advertise Find My-style functions and camera controls.
These products are particularly interesting because they go beyond simply copying the external appearance of Apple's earbuds. They attempt to introduce additional functionality that is not normally available on standard AirPods charging cases.
For example, MacRumors reported on counterfeit AirPods Pro-style earbuds with an OLED touchscreen integrated into the front of the charging case. The display offered battery information, noise control options, equalizer presets, and other functions.
Source: MacRumors – AirPods Case With Touchscreen Knock-Off Copies Apple Patent
However, there are some important limitations.
First, the presence of a touchscreen does not guarantee that every displayed feature works properly.
For example, an ANC option on the screen does not necessarily mean that the earbuds have effective active noise cancellation.
The actual experience depends on the internal chipset, microphones, firmware, speaker hardware, and software implementation.
Second, these displays should not be confused with genuine Apple hardware or Apple's original ecosystem features. A replica displaying a Find My-style interface does not mean it has genuine Apple Find My network integration.
In other words, a touchscreen can make a replica look more advanced, but it does not automatically make it a better or more reliable product.
It is another example of how sophisticated some counterfeit and imitation earbuds have become.
13. Controlling AirPods Replicas on Android With Third-Party Apps Another interesting topic of Replica Airpods is, you can find 3rd Party Applications to control and monitor battery of your Original Airpods, Replica Airpods and TWS Bluetooth Earphones. Be carefull that some of the APK's may require Root Access which is not recommended only for monitoring/controling your Airpods or reps... 
While genuine AirPods have limited functionality on Android compared with iOS, certain replica chipsets can work with dedicated companion applications that provide additional configuration options.
However, not every application supports every replica. Compatibility depends heavily on the Bluetooth chipset and firmware installed in the earbuds.
PodsBattery: Battery Monitoring for AirPods Replicas Another useful Android application is PodsBattery – AirPods battery, developed by JiShufeng.
This is the app that I used to monitor battery on my Replica Fubar Airpods 3...
Unlike applications focused mainly on chipset configuration, PodsBattery is primarily designed to monitor battery information from AirPods and compatible replica earbuds.
Its features include:
Battery pop-ups when connecting compatible earbuds
Left and right earbud battery indicators
Charging case battery information on supported models
Battery notifications in the notification bar and status bar
Home-screen widgets
Dynamic Island-style battery display
In-ear detection on supported configurations
Additional touch-control options for compatible devices
One particularly interesting detail is that the developer explicitly lists clone AirPods among the supported device categories.
However, compatibility is not guaranteed with every replica. Some clones report battery information differently from genuine AirPods, and certain features may not work correctly depending on the internal chipset and firmware.
The application may also require additional Android permissions, such as location access, depending on the features being used.
PodsBattery is therefore worth trying if your main goal is to monitor the battery levels of replica AirPods on Android. However, it should not be confused with a full chipset configuration tool: it does not universally provide advanced EQ or ANC adjustments.
You can find it on the Google Play Store – PodsBattery.
AndroPods: Battery Information and Connection Features One example is AndroPods – AirPods on Android, an Android application designed to make using AirPods more convenient on Android devices.
Andropods app for Android
Its main features include:
Battery level indicators
AirPods-style connection pop-ups
Battery notifications
Ear detection and playback pause/resume on supported configurations
Additional interaction features
It is important to understand that AndroPods is primarily a companion application. It does not automatically unlock hardware-level EQ or ANC controls on every replica.
It is also worth noting that AndroPods is designed around AirPods and compatible devices. A replica may or may not report the necessary Bluetooth information for the application to work correctly.
FlyCC: Configuration for Certain Airoha-Based Replicas Some more advanced replica platforms support dedicated applications that communicate with the earbuds' internal chipset.
For example, FlyCC is associated with certain Airoha-based Bluetooth audio platforms.
Depending on the chipset and firmware version, compatible earbuds may expose options such as:
Equalizer adjustments
Audio profile customization
ANC-related configuration
Touch control settings
Firmware update functionality
Not every Airoha-based replica supports every feature, and compatibility can vary between hardware revisions.
StarFun, BullSuper and Other Chipset-Specific Applications Other replica platforms may use different companion applications.
Examples reported in replica-focused community documentation include:
StarFun: Associated with certain Huilian-based platforms.
BullSuper: Associated with certain HR-based platforms.
KKX: Used with some specific replica hardware versions.
Behool: Associated with certain BES-based platforms.
These applications are not universal AirPods control tools. An application designed for one chipset may fail to detect earbuds using a completely different platform.
You can find a community-maintained overview of these applications and their reported compatibility here:
AirReps – Useful Apps for AirPods Replicas
Can You Adjust EQ and ANC on Android? Potentially, yes, but it depends on the earbuds.
There are two different types of audio adjustment worth understanding.
Software EQ: Android's built-in equalizer or a compatible third-party audio application can modify the sound output. This can work even when the earbuds do not support a dedicated companion application.
Samsung's Built In Software Custom EQ Settings 
Hardware-level controls: Some chipset-specific applications can communicate directly with compatible earbuds to change supported settings, including EQ profiles, ANC modes, or touch controls.
However, a generic Android EQ application cannot magically add genuine ANC to earbuds that do not have the necessary hardware.
Likewise, selecting an ANC mode in an application does not guarantee effective noise cancellation.
A Word of Caution About Third-Party Applications Many chipset-specific companion applications are distributed outside the Google Play Store.
Before installing one, check its developer, source, permissions, and compatibility with your exact earbud version.
Be particularly careful with unofficial APK downloads and firmware updates. Installing incompatible firmware can cause connectivity problems or even make the earbuds unusable.
Avoid granting unnecessary permissions or installing unknown applications simply because a seller recommends them.
The important point is that some replicas offer considerably more configuration options than their appearance initially suggests. However, these features are highly dependent on the hardware and software combination.
14. Why Legitimate Budget TWS Earbuds Are a Better Choice I am not against inexpensive wireless earbuds.
In fact, I think budget TWS products make a lot of sense for many users.
Not everyone needs premium Apple, Sony, or Samsung earbuds.
Havit TWS. Reputated and Warrantied trustable budget brand. Even this product is cheap than Replica Airpods...
If you mainly listen to music, watch videos, or make occasional phone calls, a reasonably priced pair of wireless earbuds may be more than enough.
However, there is a significant difference between an affordable legitimate product and a counterfeit imitation.
A legitimate budget TWS product can offer:
An identifiable manufacturer
More transparent specifications
A clearly defined product identity
A legitimate warranty or return process
More realistic feature descriptions
Independent reviews and comparisons
Better accountability if something goes wrong
You do not need your earbuds to pretend to be AirPods.
You need them to provide good sound, reliable connectivity, acceptable battery life, and comfortable everyday use.
In my opinion, buying a legitimate budget TWS product is a much more sensible decision than spending money on counterfeit AirPods.
The objective should be getting the best possible experience for your budget, not buying the closest possible imitation of an expensive product.
15. Are Fake AirPods Worth Buying in 2026? My answer is no. I would not recommend purchasing counterfeit AirPods.
However, I also do not want to make the inaccurate claim that every replica sounds terrible or that all of them use outdated hardware.
Some advanced replicas can provide surprisingly good audio quality and convincing iOS-style integration.
My experience with Fubar AirPods 3 is a good example.
But the initial experience is only one part of the purchasing decision.
You also need to consider battery quality, long-term reliability, software support, warranty coverage, manufacturing transparency, and product authenticity.
A replica might work well for a while, but you have little assurance about what happens when something goes wrong.
There is also no reason to support counterfeit branding when legitimate budget wireless earbuds are widely available.
If you are trying to save money, choose an affordable product that is honestly marketed for what it is.
You can find good wireless earbuds without pretending they are manufactured by Apple.
Final Thoughts: Do Not Pay for the Illusion of a Premium Product After using replica AirPods myself, my opinion is that they are not worth recommending. I live in Turkey, replica Airpods are sold with a "Bazaar Price" which starts about 7 USD (350 Turkish Lira's) up to 40 USD (2000 Turkish Lira's) maybe the most luxirous quality we can find. Average price is 10-13 USD as acceptable quality product. Theese prices are quite budget that we can try buying a fake Airpods and make it a "Junk Airpods" or maybe just for try. I still dont recommend buying fake Airpods because you can find authentic TWS for cheaper price. But in US/EU Replica airpods are more expensive then Turkey's Bazaar Price... So not worth it, just you are wasting your hard earned money. 
Some models can be surprisingly convincing. They may sound good, connect easily to Apple devices, and imitate features that were once associated only with genuine AirPods.
Some even have touchscreen charging cases or support third-party Android applications for additional controls.
But that does not make them genuine products or reliable long-term purchases.
I would rather spend my money on a legitimate budget wireless earbud from an identifiable manufacturer than purchase a counterfeit product that attempts to pass itself off as an Apple device.
This is not about saying that everyone should buy expensive premium earbuds.
Quite the opposite.
You can save money and still make a sensible purchasing decision.
My recommendation is simple: Avoid counterfeit AirPods. If you dont want or can't afford a Genuine Apple Airpods, you can get another cheap Authentic Brand... 
Good value means getting a reliable product for your money, not a product that looks expensive/luxury with cheap price. 
Frequently Asked Questions Are fake AirPods worth buying? I would not recommend them. Some replicas can offer surprisingly good sound quality, but uncertain manufacturing standards, battery reliability, warranty coverage, and long-term support make them difficult to recommend.
Are replica AirPods the same as original AirPods? No. Replica earbuds are not genuine Apple products. Similar designs, pairing animations, and battery indicators do not prove that they contain Apple's original hardware.
Why do fake AirPods appear as genuine AirPods on an iPhone? Some replicas imitate parts of Apple's Bluetooth pairing and device-identification experience through their firmware. An AirPods-style pairing animation does not prove that the earbuds contain an Apple H1 or H2 chip.
Which chipsets are used in fake AirPods? Different replica generations have been associated with chipset families such as Airoha, Huilian, BES, Jieli, and Bluetrum. The actual chipset depends on the particular model and production version.
Are Airoha or Huilian replica chipped earphones are genuine Apple products? No. Airoha and Huilian are separate chipset platforms. Their use in an earbud does not make it an authentic Apple product.
Can fake AirPods have a touchscreen charging case? As we mentioned at this article, Yes. Some modified replica models have charging cases with built-in displays. Depending on the model, they may show battery information, connection status, EQ presets, and noise control options. These features do not make the earbuds genuine Apple products.
Can I control fake AirPods on Android? Some replicas support third-party Android applications. Compatibility depends on the chipset and firmware. Applications such as FlyCC and StarFun are associated with certain chipset platforms, while AndroPods mainly provides battery information and connection-related features.
Can I adjust EQ and ANC on Android? Some compatible replicas allow EQ and ANC-related adjustments through chipset-specific applications. However, not every model supports these features, and a software setting cannot add genuine ANC hardware to earbuds that do not have it.
Are cheap TWS earbuds better than fake AirPods? A legitimate budget TWS product can be a better purchase because it has an identifiable manufacturer, clearer specifications, and potentially more dependable warranty and support options.
Can fake AirPods damage your phone? There is no reason to assume every replica will damage a smartphone. However, unknown companion apps and unnecessary permissions should be treated cautiously. Avoid installing untrusted software just to enable additional earbud features. 
Are fake AirPods safe? Safety depends on the actual hardware and manufacturing quality. Unknown battery specifications and inadequate charging protection can introduce risks. Choosing products from identifiable manufacturers is preferable.
Why are fake AirPods so cheap? They may use less expensive components, simpler manufacturing processes, and fewer quality-control and support services. Counterfeit products may also imitate Apple's branding without providing genuine Apple hardware or services.

Why You Should NOT Buy Fake AirPods in 2026: The Truth About Replica Earbuds

Fake AirPods have become increasingly sophisticated over the last few years. What once looked like an obvious cheap imitation has evolved into something much more convincing. Some replicas now feature surprisingly good sound quality, AirPods-style pairing animations, battery indicators, and even compatibility with certain Apple device features.

At first glance, buying a pair of replica AirPods for a fraction of the original price might seem like a great deal. After all, why spend a significant amount of money on genuine Apple AirPods when a much cheaper alternative appears to offer a similar experience?

I used to think about this differently as well.



I have personally owned replica AirPods, a pair of Airpods 3 with charging case, branded as “Fubar Airpods 3” bought from Turkey. Surprisingly, the experience was not entirely bad. The sound quality was quite good, and the earbuds were recognized by Apple devices almost like genuine AirPods. Also find my Apple was working when you connected the Fake Airpods 3 to an Apple Device…



However, after looking beyond the initial experience, I believe there are several important reasons why buying counterfeit AirPods is not a good decision.

This article is not about promoting replica products or recommending specific counterfeit models. Instead, I want to explain how these products work, why some of them are surprisingly convincing, what their technical limitations are, and why I would recommend choosing legitimate budget TWS earbuds instead.

1. What Are These Fake AirPods and Why They Became So Popular?

Fake AirPods are wireless earbuds designed to imitate Apple’s original AirPods. They may copy the appearance of the earbuds, charging case, packaging, product names, and even some of the software features.

You may see descriptions at online shopping stores like:

  • 1:1 AirPods replica

  • OEM AirPods

  • High-copy AirPods

  • Clone AirPods

  • Replica AirPods Pro

  • AirPods 3 replicas

These terms are often used loosely by sellers and do not necessarily describe a specific hardware platform or quality level.

It is also important to distinguish between generic TWS earbuds and counterfeit AirPods.

TWS stands for True Wireless Stereo. It simply describes wireless earbuds that operate without a cable connecting the left and right sides. TWS doesnt have any implementation made or mimic Apple Airpods Products. Just think like a classic cheap bluetooth wirelles in ear twin headphones. 

There are many legitimate manufacturers producing affordable TWS earbuds. These products may have a similar general design to AirPods without pretending to be genuine Apple products.

Counterfeit AirPods are different. They attempt to imitate Apple’s branding and product identity, potentially misleading buyers into believing that they are purchasing something manufactured or authorized by Apple.

Their popularity is understandable. Genuine AirPods can be expensive, while replicas are marketed at considerably lower prices.

But the low price does not necessarily mean good value.

2. Not All Fake AirPods Use the Same Hardware

One common misconception is that every replica AirPods model uses the same cheap Bluetooth chip and offers equally poor performance.

Inside of an Original Apple Airpods


That is not necessarily true.

The replica market has evolved, and different products can use different Bluetooth audio platforms. Some inexpensive models use basic solutions, while more sophisticated versions have been associated with chipset families such as Airoha, Huilian, and BES.

These platforms help explain why certain replicas can offer surprisingly convincing connectivity and audio features.

However, identifying and knowing the chipset alone is not enough to determine the quality and performance of an entire product itself.

Airoha Bluetooth Chipsets

Airoha is one of the manufacturers frequently mentioned in discussions about more advanced AirPods replicas.



Chipset names and variants reported in different replica generations include:

  • Airoha 1562M

  • Airoha 1562E

  • Airoha 1563E

  • Airoha 1571AM

Some community documentation associates these chipsets with different AirPods-style replica versions.

Airoha 1562A equipped replica Airpods Pro from Aliexpress


Depending on the implementation, Airoha-based platforms can offer relatively advanced Bluetooth connectivity, audio processing, power management, and support for additional features.

This is one reason why some replicas perform considerably better than basic generic Bluetooth earbuds.

However, a product using an Airoha chipset is not automatically high quality. The speaker drivers, microphones, firmware, battery cells, antenna design, and overall manufacturing process are equally important.

It is also worth noting that chipset names used in replica communities do not always correspond directly to official manufacturer product names. Exact hardware identification can vary between models and production batches.

Huilian Chipsets and Apple-Like Integration

Huilian is another chipset family that appears in discussions about more sophisticated AirPods replicas.

Names such as Huilian A10 and Huilian 247 have been associated with products offering advanced iOS-style integration.

Huilian 247 equipped Airpods Pro 3 from a Russian seller…


Some implementations reportedly support AirPods-like pairing experiences and features resembling Apple’s multi-device functionality.

This can make certain replicas surprisingly convincing when used with an iPhone.

However, similar-looking software behavior does not mean that a product has genuine Apple hardware or access to every proprietary Apple service.

BES (Bestechnic) Chipsets

BES is another manufacturer associated with Bluetooth audio platforms used in different wireless earbuds.

Examples reported in replica discussions include:

  • BES 2300ZP

  • BES 2500YP

  • BES 2600 series

Some implementations are associated with more advanced audio processing and noise-cancellation capabilities.

Nevertheless, chipset specifications alone cannot guarantee effective ANC, good microphone quality, or long-term reliability.

A poorly designed product can still perform badly even if it uses a relatively advanced Bluetooth chipset.

Jieli and Bluetrum: Other Bluetooth Solutions

Not every replica uses a relatively advanced platform.

Jieli (JL) and Bluetrum are also associated with affordable Bluetooth audio products and entry-level wireless earbuds.

These platforms can provide basic wireless audio functionality, although the actual performance depends on the complete hardware and firmware implementation.

It is important not to judge a product’s quality, performance etc… directly by its chipset. The quality matters by the whole implemention of product including chipset, speakers, microphone and the battery case. 

A cheaper Bluetooth platform does not automatically mean terrible sound quality, just as a more expensive platform does not guarantee a good listening experience.

The biggest issue is the lack of reliable information and quality control surrounding many counterfeit products.

3. How Can Fake AirPods Device Can Appear as Genuine AirPods on an iPhone?

This is probably one of the most interesting aspects of modern AirPods replicas.

If not equipped as a TWS device or any other trash quality chipsetted Airpods Replica, when you open the case of your replica Airpods, it interacts with Iphone and shows Airpods opening animation, device model (like original), device name and battery percentage…

For an inexperienced user or 3rd party inspectors, this can create the impression that the earbuds contain Apple’s original hardware.

But there is an important distinction.

An iPhone device displaying an AirPods-style openning and pairing window does not prove that the earbuds contain an Apple H1 or H2 chip. Shortly doesnt mean that Airpods device is original. 

A seller showing Replica Airpods Pro connected to An Iphone device with Airpods Pairing Animation…


Certain Bluetooth/Wifi implementations and mimiced design of hardware/firmware configurations can imitate parts of an Original Apple Airpods and device-identification…

This is why some replicas can appear surprisingly authentic during initial setup.

However, genuine AirPods offer much deeper integration with Apple’s ecosystem.

For example, seeing an AirPods-style pairing animation does not establish that a replica has:

  • Genuine Apple H1 or H2 hardware

  • Full Apple Find My network integration

  • Genuine iCloud device association

  • All original AirPods software features

  • The same security and authentication mechanisms

A familiar interface is not proof of authenticity.

Also dont forget that some non cheap priced AirPods Replicas come with Magsafe support but still this doesnt mean that Replica Airpods do include Original Apple Hardware. Dont forget that these specifications can be replicated with low prices today…

This is also why I would never recommend buying a product simply because an online seller demonstrates an iPhone pairing animation in a promotional video.

4. My Personal Experience With Replica Fubar AirPods 3

I want to mention my own experience because not every replica experience is necessarily terrible.

I previously owned a pair of Fubar AirPods 3, and honestly, I was surprised by their performance.

The sound quality was quite good, especially considering that they were not genuine Apple products. Sadly microphone quality was trash, but I do use phone’s own microphone during daily talks and other jobs… 

Another interesting aspect was their compatibility with Apple devices. During pairing, they were recognized almost like original AirPods, providing a familiar experience that was considerably more convincing than what I expected from a cheap imitation.

This is an important distinction.

I am not claiming that every fake AirPods product has terrible sound quality or that every replica is unusable.

Some versions can offer a surprisingly decent experience, particularly when they use more advanced Bluetooth audio platforms.

HDD vs SSD vs NVMe in 2025: Are Hard Drives Still Worth Using for Gaming & Storage? In a gaming and computer processing world dominated by blazing fast SATA SSDs and a few times more quicker, ultra fast NVMe drives, we may think that hard disk drives (HDDs) have been left in the past. But still today, there are still some people use it fore some reasons we will explain at this post.
If you are a gamer on a budget, storing/managing large libraries or work on reviving an old system, using HDD is still viable solution for this system with right expectation... Also can be better with some optimizations...
In this post we will talk about HDD's today's situation and its comparisons with SSD, according to the performance and affordability issues, and how we can get the best possible experience from a setup with HDD, what we will expect in terms of performance and price.
Since almost every PC users and producers have switched to NVME SSD's, HDD have became a side/background storage device instead of main OS/Program device... Some of hosting companies use HDD for light hosting. Also you can boot light, old or indie games with small size from HDD without any lags...
HDD vs SSD: Why SSDs Became the Standard SSD (Solid State Drives) are researched and developed to go beyond the speed/latency limits of Hard Disk Drives have. HDD's do work based on spinning magnetic disk and mechanical moving parts which have latency multiple times slower and delayed with respect to SSD's. But HDD's do have larger capacities per price rate. HDD has longer boot time, slower read/write speed and has risk of mechanical failure especially can happen in case of portable devices like laptop...
SSD's use flash memory chips without no any parts (as in HDD we have rotating disks and rotating readers...)... SSD's were invented to deliver faster data read/write. It is also better energy efficient for our computing needs for both daily tasks and other entertaining or productive things that need system performance, disk write/read operations...
By the time, SSD's became the a bit expensive but valuable solution for speeding up loading time of OS/apps, totally increasing the overall system performance and visual experience smoothness... Also we know that SSD's are mainly developed to increase the speed of Laptops. As we know laptops do have limited CPU/Ram and Bus speeds because of power consumption needs... SSD's do relax the I/O operations in laptops. 
Primary Uses of HDDs in 2025 1. Mass Storage / Archiving HDDs offer slow but heavy large capacities (up to 20TB and higher) at a much lower price per gigabyte than SSDs. This makes them the best solution for:
Backup drives that keep systems or databases backups that can be accessible... File servers that keep important files online/restricted... Personal cloud storage Local NAS (Network Attached Storage) systems 2. Budget Builds & Entry-Level PCs In cheapo/light budget PCs and laptops, they cannot locate big amount of money to storage so HDD's are included as main storage or secondary larger storage. Theese can be:
For storing media files, documents, and non-performance requiring software/games... Daily home tasks like video etc.. Smaller SSD can be used for Operating System only, and other programs that doesnt require fast storage. Can be combined with HDD... 3. Surveillance Systems Security cameras do record heavy videos that are important and need heavy amount of storage. Also theese need to be safe... HDDs are still the preferred storage solution for:
DVR/NVR systems  Continuous live video recording like cctv Archieves, backups... 4. Gaming Libraries (Secondary Storage) Gamers often install older games or the games that keep at their pc as Junk, may move their games from SSD to HDD... Many still use HDDs for:
Steam/Origin/Epic game libraries MMO or open-world games with large install sizes but minimal I/O needs (for example older RPG Games) Games with extra large of community DLC/Mods but may need little amount of read/write speeds. People may not spend their SSD's space for mods and too many DLC's... DLC/Mod users can download mods freely to HDD.  Developers included game developers that store/keep older versions of high size of games/applications they developed...  5. Data Centers (Cold Storage) While SSDs dominate high-speed server workloads, HDDs are still used in data centers for:
Cold storage (infrequently accessed data but needs to be safely stored)  Archieve storages Video/media storage at high scale Statistical Comparison: HDD vs SSD vs NVMe What is an HDD? HDD is cheap and slow solution. But more safe...
As we talk for security of data: Even mechanism, chips etc... get broken on HDD, you can save data in spinning platter (disc). This makes the HDD as easier for data recovery in case of mechanical or chip failure of the drive.
Speed: ~80–160 MB/s (slowest) Technology: Mechanical parts (spinning platter + moving head) Price: Cheapest per GB Lifespan: Good, but prone to mechanical failure over time Best For: Mass storage Backup systems and manually storing Backup Data's, Backup, Database Backup Sequental Image Files... Movie/Music/Image media libraries  Light Budget PCs What is an SSD? (SATA SSD) SSD (Solid State Drive) uses flash memory chips (usually SATA-based but has NAND too) and has no mechanical moving parts. It’s significantly faster than HDD but can be less reliable...
It is hard, maybe almost near impossible, expensive to save data from a dead ssd, making it unsafe to save data's, according to HDD. Also SSD's are more sensitive to Statical Electric which can cause failure more in SSD's. Statical Electric can cause the passing electric inside circuits to short...
Speed: ~500–550 MB/s (SATA SSD). SATA SSDs use NAND flash memory (just like other SSDs) but uses SATA III interface for data transfer, which has a maximum speed of 6 Gbps (~550 MB/s in real-world use). It may be limited speed because of SATA III interface. Some low GB Sata SSD's have lower write speeds down to 150 MB/s... Even you have the Fastest chip, SATA interface will limit your speed. It is the same interface as latest Hard Drives.  Technology: NAND Flash via SATA interface same as Modern Hard Drives... Price: High Per GB, since Sata SSD's are demanding low, a bit cheaper that NVME drives... Lifespan: Normally longer than HDD, but can suddenly fail because of short cut... What is NVMe SSD?
NVMe (Non-Volatile Memory Express) is the newest type of SSD that has direct connection between motherboard and SSD. By the direct connection through PCIe slot, it bypasses the SATA interface's bandwith limitation. Having almost 10-15 times faster transfer speed and lower delay than SATA SSD. 
Speed: 3,000–7,000+ MB/s (fastest SSD solution). Speeds may change according to the Pci-e version (3.0-5.0) Technology: NAND Flash via higher speed and low latency PCIe interface connected directly to the motherboard Price: Higher per GB (prices are fluctiating according to the demand/production) Lifespan: Similar to SATA SSDs, but varies by quality, brand and type of Flash Chip used... Best For: High end gaming Video editing, 3D rendering that needs to write the rendered image models to the disk or read... Multitasking power users Modern laptops and gaming rigs SSD Timeline Early 1990s: SSD and its other like technologies used in military and enterprise. Mid–2000s: First PC style consumer SSDs (very expensive, low capacity) started using. 2010s onward: Production of SSD's do incerase and price starts dropping to the daily budgets, mainstream adoption in PCs and laptops have increased. Today (2025): SSD's are now the standard for PC's. NVME drives do dominate the market because of its ultra fast speeds. Scenario On HDD On SSD (SATA/NVMe) Open-world games (e.g., GTA V, RDR2) Texture streaming causes lag stutter & hitches Smoother asset loading = higher 0.1% lows First-time area loads Hangs or freezes during loading Faster transitions, fewer drops Heavy multiplayer games (Warzone, Apex) Disk can't keep up with streaming pace Consistent frame pacing Games using DirectStorage (e.g., Forspoken) Frequently bottlenecked by HDD speed Vastly better 0.1% lows with NVMe SSDs Real-World FPS Benchmarks (Approximated) Cyberpunk 2077 Avg FPS 1% Low 0.1% Low HDD 60 FPS 40 FPS 15 FPS (Stutter) SATA SSD 60 FPS 50 FPS 30 FPS NVMe SSD 60 FPS 55 FPS 48 FPS (Smooth) Final Thoughts: Is HDD Still Worth It in 2025? For extreme budget/cheap systems, since the performance is ignored, the HDD can be used. But giving just a little budget for small ssd can be good... Also for backups, NAS systems, storages, and systems that used as a GIT, HDD can be the solution with cheap and large solution.

Today, the most balanced setup for many users is using an SSD or NVMe drive for both operating system, productivity, and gaming... Also keeping an HDD for large file storage, backup and archives.
